newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Reforms will bring social problems - Romanian leader.
newsitem.headline: Reforms will bring social problems - Romanian leader.

text.p: Economic reforms will bring social problems to Romania over the next five months, the country's new President Emil Constantinescu was quoted as saying on Thursday.
Asked whether Romania's economic reform programme would spark social instability, Constantinescu told Publico newspaper in an interview: "Yes. It will create social problems."

"We are warning that there will be a difficult period for five months, and so we will establish a social pact with representatives of trade unions and civilian society," he said during a trip to Lisbon this week.
"We must be aware that there will be a price to pay at the social level," he added. Constantinescu was elected President of Romania last month, ousting ex-communists.
"Our programme includes genuine economic reform, rapid privatisations, support for foreign investment with adequate legislation and a drastic struggle against corruption," Constantinescu said.

The government, made up of Constantinescu's centrist Democratic Convention, Social Democrats and representatives of the 1.6 million Hungarian minority, is to present short and long-term economic programmes to parliament this week.
The Convention's electoral programme called for budget discipline tempered by increased benefits for the needy.
Constantinescu visited Lisbon to attend a conference of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Monday and Tuesday.
